headline: Homebuilders and Healthcare Lead a Broad Tuesday Advance
body_html:
Stocks finished Tuesday's session with a wide advance. Of the 544 names we track, 395 rose and 147 fell. The move was driven by many stocks rather than a few large ones, and it extended the push for back-to-back gains that traders had been discussing going into the day.

The rotation was clear. Homebuilders led every group with a 2.62% gain, followed by healthcare at 2.05% and software at 1.7%. Consumer shares added 1.04%, industrials 0.61% and materials 0.54%. Semiconductors rose a modest 0.48% and lagged the field. Energy was the only group to slip, down 0.07%, even with a steady flow of Middle East headlines.

The standout mover was eXp World Holdings, up 8.72%, with Sarepta Therapeutics close behind at 8.46% and Verra Mobility up 7.65%. The weakness sat in industrial and infrastructure-linked names: Mueller Industries fell 6.93%, Genuine Parts 5.45% and Comfort Systems USA 4.8%. Winners clearly outnumbered losers, so the question for Wednesday, October 21, is whether this rotation holds or the laggards claw back some ground.

briefs.headline: Boeing Clears a Long-Awaited Regulatory Hurdle
briefs.body: U.S. aviation regulators have approved the 737 Max 10, ending a wait of several years for the largest variant of Boeing's narrow-body family. The decision removes a major uncertainty for the planemaker and for airlines that have been waiting on the jet.

briefs.headline: Apple Win Puts Qnity in the Spotlight
briefs.body: Qnity is reported to have landed iPhone-related business from Apple. For a supplier, a place in that product chain can bring both volume and credibility. Investors will want to see how large the contract becomes once the details emerge.

briefs.headline: Anthropic Said to Weigh Another Big Compute Deal
briefs.body: Anthropic is reportedly in talks with the specialty cloud provider Nscale on a second multibillion-dollar agreement. If it goes ahead, it would show that demand for AI computing capacity is still pulling in outside infrastructure providers.

briefs.headline: Biotech Names Pace the Healthcare Rally
briefs.body: Healthcare gained 2.05% on the session, and two biotech companies were among the biggest individual winners. Sarepta Therapeutics rose 8.46% and argenx climbed 6.48%. Their gains helped the sector rank second among the groups we follow.

briefs.headline: Industrial and Infrastructure Names Take the Hits
briefs.body: Several industrial stocks tied to building and power were the session's biggest decliners. Mueller Industries dropped 6.93%, Comfort Systems USA lost 4.8% and Forgent Power Solutions fell 4.44%. Their weakness stood out against a market in which most stocks rose.

briefs.headline: Tehran Holds Firm on Talks With Washington
briefs.body: Iran has reportedly told Pakistan's army chief it will not hold talks with Washington until its demands are met. Separately, Britain said it will fly defensive air missions over Saudi Arabia. Energy shares still slipped 0.07%, the only sector decline of the day.
